[[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado Brotherhood]] |rank =Elder |location =[[Coronado]] |status = |dod = |dod verified= |titles = |family = |TV actor =[[Brian Thompson]] }} The '''Coronado elder''' is a leader of the [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado chapter]] of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]]. ==Background== He is evidently considered an ally by [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]] of the [[Knights of San Fernando]], to the point of being included as a prospective supporter for a civil war against the dominant [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth chapter]], which Quintus claims "only takes and gives nothing in return." The Coronado elder seems rough and carries himself sternly. However, he is also confrontational and patriarchal, even to his fellow chapter leaders, making a misogynistic comment towards the female [[McRae|Elder McRae]] and calling out the [[Grand Canyon elder]] for his lackluster attitude, belittling him as a "yahoo." He is a tall, large man with a stern face and short gray hair. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Golden Rule]]=== The Coronado elder, as well as the [[Yosemite elder|Yosemite chapter's elder]] and the [[Grand Canyon elder|Grand Canyon chapter's elder]], arrive at [[Area 51]] via [[Brotherhood airship|airship]] to meet with Elder Cleric Quintus to hear his overtures for a new "axis of power" in the Brotherhood. The Coronado elder eats food with a fork while listening to Quintus' proposition with a skeptical glance. He interrupts Quintus to point out the Commonwealth chapter's absence, which leads Quintus to angrily claim that the Commonwealth chapter would simply take the [[cold fusion]] diode they had obtained. After a brief tirade by the Grand Canyon elder, the Coronado and Yosemite elders express wariness about sparking a civil war with the Commonwealth, though Quintus tries to convince them that the cold fusion diode will give them the edge. The Yosemite elder remarks on how their chapters have drifted apart, and the Coronado elder immediately insults her by insinuating that she would not be allowed to voice her thoughts in the Coronado chapter. When the Grand Canyon elder claims to enjoy autonomy granted by the Commonwealth, he insults them by claiming they enjoy the freedom to "fuck robots." He then complains about having wasted resources to come to the meeting and insults the Grand Canyon elder as a "yahoo," but is silenced by Quintus, who hauls over crates of [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]]s to demonstrate the potential of the cold fusion diode. The Coronado elder lifts one of the cores out of a crate and is left stunned at the sight. All three elders soon agree to the alliance with Quintus, and they celebrate with a toast. Later, all of the elders watch as two [[Knight (TV series)|knights]] fight each other for their entertainment. The Coronado elder remains stern, but visibly expresses approval during the fight, lighting a cigar and throwing small air punches. He also watches [[Maximus]]' fight with a [[Coronado knight|knight from his chapter]], lighting another cigar when the knight gives Maximus a beatdown; his reactions after the fight turns deadly are not seen. When [[Xander Harkness|Paladin Xander Harkness]] unexpectedly arrives soon after, the Coronado elder stands warily, putting his cigar in his mouth as Quintus "welcomes" the Commonwealth liaison to their meeting. ===[[The Demon in the Snow]]=== As Elder McRae is attempting to make a deal with Paladin Harkness (actually the mutated [[Thaddeus]] in disguise), the Coronado elder interrupts, suspecting her of trying to sacrifice the other chapters to the Commonwealth's wrath for supporting Quintus. He insults McRae's womanhood again, then attempts to offer his own deal to the Commonwealth emissary, trading Quintus's head for a supply of fusion cores while remarking that his chapter came to the meeting expecting to fight the others eventually. As he and McRae quarrel, the Grand Canyon elder bursts into the mess hall, loudly accusing the other elders of stealing the cold fusion relic that went missing, actually stolen by [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]]. The Coronado elder attempts to contact his airship crew to suit up, but is stabbed in the mouth through his cheeks and severing his tongue by McRae who pulled a knife behind him. The Grand Canyon elder exclaims that it was "cool" before the various chapters break out into fighting. ==Notes== The Coronado elder's armor appears similar to the [[science scribe's armor]] from ''[[Fallout 76]]''; whether this is indicative of his former rank before becoming elder is unclear. ==Appearances== The Coronado elder appears only {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|10=202|12=204}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Brotherhood of Steel characters]] [[ru:Старейшина Коронадского Братства Стали]]
